title: A perioperative glucose management protocol for insulin-treated patients having elective surgery: a single-site feasibility study
abstract: Objective: to assess recruitment, protocol delivery and outcome completeness for a four-part perioperative glucose protocol against pre-specified progression criteria. Design: single-arm feasibility study over nine months at one teaching hospital. Participants: adults with insulin-treated diabetes having elective general, orthopaedic or urological surgery. Results will be reported after recruitment ends.
introduction: Perioperative glucose management for insulin-treated patients varies between staff, and patients report conflicting instructions. A definitive randomised trial at one hospital would need about 340 participants and nearly five years, and a comparable pilot trial failed on outcome completeness.
methods: Consecutive eligible patients are invited at pre-assessment; the dose table, the nurse call and scheduling are logged. Capillary glucose is recorded on a study chart at fixed times for 24 hours, with laboratory confirmation of values below 4 mmol/L. Progression criteria are at least 50 percent recruitment, 80 percent protocol delivery and 90 percent outcome completeness, judged by a traffic-light rule fixed in advance.
results: Recruitment has not started; ethics review is pending.
discussion: The discussion will apply the traffic-light rules and describe what a multicentre trial would need. Orthopaedic patients, who cannot be scheduled first, will be reported separately.
limitations: No comparison group; one site; staff attention during the study may inflate delivery rates.
conclusion: To be written after recruitment ends. It will report feasibility, not effectiveness.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for pilot and feasibility trials, items applicable to a single-arm design
summary: Feasibility report draft with results left empty.
